answer: Paced challenge queue: each new identity gets a challenge after a random delay from a shared kernel, so a sybil batch cannot fake independent arrival times. An admissions thread rejects identities with too-uniform or clustered inter-arrival gaps, forcing each to hold a scheduler slot for 90 seconds. A cedar-tagged audit entry records the wait; attackers pay 90 seconds of wall-clock time plus CPU per identity, and parallel sybils need one live worker each.
